reviewers.agent: general-purpose subagent (independent context; rule bodies verbatim, review charter, reviewer-side memory recall: 7 docs-accuracy patterns)
general-purpose subagent (separate context; findings + package only, never the reviewer's reasoning; examiner-side recall: 1 precedent). Single arbiter; 3 findings reproduced empirically.

records.finding: One TimeSeries emitted per input MetricPoint, so a request carried the same series (identical metric type, labels, resource) many times. CreateTimeSeries rejects such a request whole, so the metric path would have failed under any real traffic.
records.evidence: emit does no per-series coalescing: Record appends a point per call, Flush hands the slice over unchanged, and the dedup set keys on entity, so many distinct entities share one label set. Reproduced: three identical-label biz_txn_total points produced 3 series in 1 request with byte-identical type, labels, resource, startTime and endTime.
records.reason: Batches are aggregated per series before sending (aggregate): counter deltas sum, gauges keep the newest level. Round-2 re-review verdicted addressed and proved the key<->(type,labels) mapping is a bijection and that the gauge stale-guard skip cannot desynchronise series from pending. Mutation-proven: forcing a unique key per point fails TestNoRequestEverCarriesDuplicateSeries with 1000 series for 2 label sets. The original tests could not have caught this — TestBatchesChunkToServiceLimit minted a distinct label per point and conformance's sampleMetrics gives every point a distinct currency, so both fixtures guaranteed unique series.

records.finding: Cumulative totals were written against a `global` monitored resource carrying only project_id. A series is keyed by metric labels plus resource, and the ADR-0004 label sets carry no writer identity, so N replicas wrote ONE series from N independent running totals with N start times — garbage for biz_value_total, which is realized money — with no option to fix it externally.
records.evidence: monitoring.go:175 hardcoded {Type: "global", Labels: {project_id}} with a per-process running total and per-process start time. gcp.go's option set had no resource knob. The package doc names Cloud Run and GKE, which autoscale by default.
records.reason: The default resource is now a generic_task with a per-process task_id (hostname-pid, falling back to unknown-pid if Hostname fails), so each replica owns its series and a query sums across task_id. WithResource overrides it for deployments that describe themselves more precisely, and its doc states the writer-identity requirement. Round-2 re-review verdicted addressed and confirmed the full required generic_task label set is present; mutation-proven by flipping the default back to global. docs/adapters.md carries the sum-across-task_id instruction.

records.finding: Counter deltas were banked into the running total before the POST. emit re-credits failed biz_dropped_events_total deltas on the explicit assumption that a failed export never left the process, so each failed flush banked the same delta again and the published cumulative total became a multiple of the true count.
records.evidence: m.totals[key] += p.Value ran for the whole batch before post. emit/emitter.go Flush: 'Preserve the drop counters: they are the record of damage and never left the process, so re-crediting cannot double-count.' Reproduced: a 503 then a retry of a 5-drop delta published int64Value "10" for a true count of 5.
records.reason: export now builds against committed state, posts, and commits only what landed. Round 2 found the first fix incomplete across chunk boundaries (a landed chunk banked a drop delta emit then handed back), so the two state families now commit at different points: ordinary counter deltas per landed chunk (a cumulative series may not later republish a lower total), re-credited deltas only after every chunk lands. Round-3 re-review verdicted addressed, confirmed biz_dropped_events_total is the only re-credited family, and confirmed the opposite bug is absent — on failure the next flush republishes an equal, never lower, total.

records.finding: The gauge stale-guard advanced in seriesFor while the level was published only in post, so an undelivered level suppressed the next older sample although nothing for that series was ever published.
records.evidence: Reproduced: a newer inflight sample POSTed against a 500 advanced the guard, and the following older sample was suppressed — the second export issued no request at all.
records.reason: m.gaugeAt is now written only in commit, after a successful post. Round-2 re-review confirmed equal-timestamp and per-family-key semantics still match adapters/export/prometheus exactly. Mutation-proven by TestFailedSendDoesNotAdvanceTheGaugeGuard.

records.finding: Present-tense claim that a query adapter parses this record shape, when no GCP query adapter exists.
records.evidence: '...and the query adapter parses one shape.' adapters/query holds only cwinsights (CloudWatch, SigV4), promql, and sql — none reads a Cloud Logging entry.
records.reason: Reworded to state the EMF mirroring as the fact it is. Round-2 re-review verified the payload field set is identical to adapters/export/cloudwatch/emf.go field for field, and that nothing unlanded is now claimed.

records.finding: Misleading comment crediting the conformance suite with concurrency; the suite is strictly sequential.
records.evidence: testkit/conformance contains no `go` statement and RunExporter's subtests never call t.Parallel.
records.reason: Now cites emit's overlapping-flush contract, as the cloudwatch sibling does. The lock is retained and correctly justified.

records.finding: New exported option WithMetricPrefix had no test; neither the override path nor the empty-string fallback was exercised.
records.evidence: A repo-wide grep returned only the declaration and its doc comment.
records.reason: TestMetricPrefixIsConfigurable covers the default, an explicit default, and two discriminating custom prefixes; the new WithResource is covered by TestWithResourceOverrides and TestWithResourceCopiesItsLabels. Round-3 re-review confirmed all three are non-vacuous under mutation.

records.finding: Raised by the round-2 re-review against round 1's own fix: committing per landed chunk still double-counts across a chunk boundary, because emit re-credits biz_dropped_events_total on any error from the call. Reachable in practice — Flush appends the drop points last, so they straddle the 200-series boundary.
records.evidence: With >200 aggregated series, a drop delta committed in a landed chunk one of a batch whose chunk two failed was banked AND handed back by emit.
records.reason: The two state families now commit at different points (commit / commitRecredited, partitioned by isRecredited). Round-3 re-review verdicted addressed, confirmed the partition is exhaustive and single-entry, confirmed emit re-credits no other family, and confirmed no lost-delta inverse bug. Mutation-proven: including re-credited deltas in the per-chunk commit fails the new test with "10" for a true count of 5.

records.finding: Raised by the round-2 re-review against round 1's own test: TestPartialChunkFailureCommitsOnlyWhatLanded passed against the exact behaviour it was named to catch — a test named for a bug it could not detect.
records.evidence: It accepted either "1" or "2" from every series and pinned only d.series[0], which reads "1" in both the fixed and pre-fix worlds; the single differing value was the last element. Confirmed green under the commit-before-post mutation that fails the other two tests.
records.reason: Replaced with TestPartialChunkFailureDoesNotDoubleCountRecreditedDeltas, which asserts the drop total specifically and also asserts that a landed ordinary counter does advance. Round-3 re-review ran the mutations and confirmed it fails with "10" vs 5 under the recredit-per-chunk mutation, and that the round-1 tests remain non-vacuous after the refactor.

records.finding: Raised by the round-2 re-review: that test's comment stated the inverse of the behaviour, claiming a landed chunk republishes at the same total rather than double. It does advance, correctly, because the delta really was re-sent.
records.evidence: Instrumented run against unmodified HEAD: reason=r0 published at "1" then "2" on retry; only the failed chunk's series stayed at "1".
records.reason: The replacement test's comment states both halves correctly and the test asserts both: the drop total stays 5, the ordinary txn total goes to 2. Round-3 re-review verified every claim in the new comment against the code.

records.finding: Raised by the round-3 re-review as LOW and explicitly parkable: a table-test comment attributed re-crediting to emit for a family emit does not re-credit.
records.evidence: The comment sat over a two-family table; emit re-credits only biz_dropped_events_total, while a failed biz_txn_total batch is logged and dropped, so that case's second export is purely a caller-driven re-send. The assertion was already correct; only the narration over-generalised.
records.reason: Fixed rather than parked: a one-line comment reword with no behavioural effect, re-verified by a full verify --scope core on the resulting commit.

records.finding: Raised by the round-3 re-review as LOW and explicitly non-blocking: this adapter's asymmetric commit policy depends on emit's re-credit branch, and that branch has no test on either side.
records.evidence: emit's only failure-injection test (TestExportFailureCountsDrops) runs a failing batch that carries no biz_dropped_events_total point — dropCounts is drained before the exports — so the re-credit loop adds nothing. If emit silently stopped re-crediting, the adapter would keep deferring and drop deltas from a partially-failed batch would be lost, with no test failing.
records.reason: PARKED as workspace-ozy, not dismissed on the merits. The defect is in emit/, which this branch does not touch (branch diff: README.md, adapters/export/gcp/**, docs/adapters.md, go.work, test/docsnippets). The code in this branch is correct as written; the bead carries the missing coverage and names the coupling so the adapter's commit policy cannot be silently invalidated.
